ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a schematic diagram of the human circulatory system. There are red and blue-green blood vessels in the body; red represents arteries, and blue-green represents veins. Multiple letters in the figure use black indicator lines to label different blood vessels or structures. The letter I is located beside the right side of the human torso, and its indicator line points to a thick red vertical blood vessel in the center of the chest and abdomen. This blood vessel extends downward from near the heart, passes through the abdomen, and branches below to lead to both legs. Reasoning: According to the convention of circulatory system diagrams, red blood vessels represent arteries. The main large artery in the human body that starts from the heart and runs downward along the torso is the aorta. Therefore, the letter I labels the aorta.
